note: Targets for the visual scorecard (tools/look/score.py). Every value is a starting value: it cites LOOK.md section 7 for what it guards and is to be tightened when the owner supplies references (LOOK.md 8) and the first improvements land. A target that every shot passes is too loose.

checks.source: starting value: at most 10% of lit pixels above S 0.85 (HSV); LOOK.md 7 'saturation histogram vs palette limits'; palette limit not yet set by the owner
starting value: p95 saturation of lit pixels <= 0.90; LOOK.md 7
starting value: (p95-p5 luminance)/255 >= 0.35 on world shots; LOOK.md 7 'luminance contrast and shadow coverage'
starting value: creature pixels (p95-p5)/255 >= 0.30 at every time of day; LOOK.md 7 and 5 (subtle rim, readable night)
starting value: at most 25% of creature pixels at luminance <= 12 ('readable night', LOOK.md 3)
starting value: at most 5% of world pixels crushed (luminance <= 12); LOOK.md 7
starting value: at most 2% of pixels clipped to white (luminance >= 250); LOOK.md 7 'clipped-highlight fraction'
starting value: mean |L - blur1(L)| < 6 grey levels at 1280x720; LOOK.md 7 'high-frequency energy at game distance'
starting value: same limit on creature pixels (silhouette edges included, so loose)
starting value: p99 of |Laplacian| >= 120 by day (dawn, midday, dusk); LOOK.md 7 sharpness
starting value: max normalised 2-D autocorrelation of the detrended ground strip at lags >= 32 px < 0.30; LOOK.md 7 'repetition detection on wide shots'
starting value: under 1% of creature pixels are white specular glints (V>0.95, S<0.2); LOOK.md 7 (full check is specular/roughness range per material, not measurable from an image)

checks.source: starting value: |mean L of the creature - mean L of the ring around it|/255 >= 0.10 at strategic zoom; LOOK.md 5 'creature-vs-ground value contrast'

checks.failure: Low tier is not the same game
checks.source: starting value: mean |difference| of 32x18 luminance thumbnails low vs medium < 0.10; LOOK.md 6

checks.source: starting value: dawn and dusk are at least 5% warmer (mean R/B) than midday; LOOK.md 3 'warm dawn and dusk'

not_measurable: Plastic shine as specular/roughness per material (needs the material parameters, only a glint-fraction proxy is measured)
Black cartoon outlines (never used; no check)
Creature skin wet/matte rules (LOOK.md 4): a design rule, not an image statistic
Frame time is wall clock on software GL under a shared CPU (llvmpipe): informational and only comparable between runs on a similarly loaded machine; it does not show real GPU fps
Sun direction and terrain light are fixed by the hero look: dawn and dusk differ only by sky/cloud tint and the creature light, so the light-per-time-of-day checks measure what the game does today
Creature close-ups are on the studio preview stage (CreaturePreview) with the game's day_night light numbers, not inside the island; the game's own terrain bounce and fog are absent
